subject: Fitting no error and signal SPDE models

messages.author: 276f03e6e2cb0151
messages.subject: Fitting no error and signal SPDE models
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to fit some SPDE geostatistical models in INLA and I would like to make sure I am fitting the correct models.

I have been able to successly run an SPDE INLA model using the following formula:

formula = resp ~ 0 + b0 + x1 + x2 + f(s, model=spde)

My understanding is that this models regression coefficients for covariates b0 (intercept in my case), x1, and x2, and a spatial random field (the spde part).

Some questions about the formula:

1.  Does this formula have INLA model a "nugget" effect automatically?
2.  If not, how would I fit a "signal" model?  More specifically, using a latent structure, suppose we observe Y(s) = Z(s) + e(s) where Z(s) is the true, but unobserved response of interest and e(s) is measurement error.  How would I model Z(s)?
3.  If it does include the nugget effect automatically (and referring to the notation of question 2), is it fitting a model for Y(s) or Z(s)?  If the model is for Y(s), is there a way to model Z(s)?
4.  Lastly, if my model formula does model a nugget effect automatically, how do I fit a model with no error?

I apologize if these are easy errors.  I have looked at lots of documentation, and none of these answers were completely clear to me.

Thank you for your help.

Joshua

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting no error and signal SPDE models
parts:
On 03/04/14 00:11, Joshua French wrote:
> formula = resp ~ 0 + b0 + x1 + x2 + f(s, model=spde)
>
> My understanding is that this models regression coefficients for
> covariates b0 (intercept in my case), x1, and x2, and a spatial random
> field (the spde part).

> Some questions about the formula:
>
> 1. Does this formula have INLA model a "nugget" effect automatically?
> 2. If not, how would I fit a "signal" model? More specifically, using
> a latent structure, suppose we observe Y(s) = Z(s) + e(s) where Z(s) is
> the true, but unobserved response of interest and e(s) is measurement
> error. How would I model Z(s)?

I'll answer this together; observation noise is not (ordinarily)
specified in the formula, but rather in the observation likelihood
family in the inla() call. family="gaussian" gives Normal observation
noise, which is indistinguishable from a "nugget effect". One can also
have an explicit iid random effects term in the formula, but that gives
an unidentifiable model unless special structure is imposed.

(Also, while it's common to write "e(s)" for the measurement error in
spatial models, it's usually "e_i", i.e. tied to the observations and
not the locations as such;
otherwise two observations in the same location would have the same
measurement noise; in practice local small-scale variation is lumped
into the measurement noise, making the case less clear.)

> 3. If it does include the nugget effect automatically (and referring to
> the notation of question 2), is it fitting a model for Y(s) or Z(s)? If
> the model is for Y(s), is there a way to model Z(s)?

All the right-hand side items in the model are like "Z(s)". Think
"hierarchical model and latent/hidden field model", and _not_ "this is
a model for the observations".
See the the spde tutorial texts for more precise definitions of the
linear predictors in the spatial model case.

> 4. Lastly, if my model formula does model a nugget effect
> automatically, how do I fit a model with no error?

You can specify a known fixed (and large) precision for the Gaussian
observation likelihood model in the prior specification for that in the
inla() call with the control.family parameter.
However, the numercis can be a bit unstable for this unless the
observations are at mesh nodes only.

Finn

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting no error and signal SPDE models
parts:
On Thursday, April 3, 2014, Joshua French <joshua...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

I'm trying to fit some SPDE geostatistical models in INLA and I would like to make sure I am fitting the correct models.

I have been able to successly run an SPDE INLA model using the following formula:

formula = resp ~ 0 + b0 + x1 + x2 + f(s, model=spde)

My understanding is that this models regression coefficients for covariates b0 (intercept in my case), x1, and x2, and a spatial random field (the spde part).

Some questions about the formula:

1.  Does this formula have INLA model a "nugget" effect automatically?

We do everything in a hierarchical way (see, for instance, Banerjee, Carlin and Gelfand's book) and to be honest, I never remember which one is supposed to be the nugget. 

If you want an extra I.i,d, random effect on top of the formula above, add
... + f(loc, model="iid")
Which adds iid noise with a common unknown variance

If you want to observe the model indirectly, it's all in the likelihood. The option family="Gaussian" in the inla() call will give you the "signal model" with Z(s) given by the formula. 

So I think that answers your first 3 questions. 

For the fourth, you need to set the parameters in control.family. There should be sufficient help.  You need to fix the precision in the likelihood ("family") to be high. You need to set something in there to be =list(initial=1e5, fixed=TRUE), but I don't totally remember what. 

A lot of excellent information about the types of models we're fitting is in the spde tutorial on the r-inla web page. 

Best wishes,

Dan

2.  If not, how would I fit a "signal" model?  More specifically, using a latent structure, suppose we observe Y(s) = Z(s) + e(s) where Z(s) is the true, but unobserved response of interest and e(s) is measurement error.  How would I model Z(s)?

3.  If it does include the nugget effect automatically (and referring to the notation of question 2), is it fitting a model for Y(s) or Z(s)?  If the model is for Y(s), is there a way to model Z(s)?
4.  Lastly, if my model formula does model a nugget effect automatically, how do I fit a model with no error?

I apologize if these are easy errors.  I have looked at lots of documentation, and none of these answers were completely clear to me.

Thank you for your help.

Joshua

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Fitting no error and signal SPDE models
parts:
Ah. There it is. In the inla() call use

control.family=list(hyper=list(prec=list(initial=1e5, fixed=TRUE)))
